public_rationale: The evidence supports a real reliability concern: ACCORD finds commonsense reasoning degrading sharply with complexity. Other studies also show partial physical competence and learned world-related representations. These findings do not establish the broad claim about what ordinary training supplies by itself across all three areas. They also make a literal 'no capability at all' reading unfair.
limitations: The wording supplies no common reliability threshold.
Multimodal models and earlier experiments are context, not decisive evidence for the defined scope.
Observed failures do not prove that a particular additional architecture is necessary.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs do not provide commonsense reasoning, physical reasoning or world models for free.

statement.excerpt: Once again you eventually come around to what Ernie and I have argued all along, now believing that LLMs (our most effective known uses of big activity vectors combined with big weight matrices) give you none of that for free.
statement.document_title: Open letter responding to Yann LeCun

from_speaker: give you none of that for free
commonsense, physical reasoning or world models
our_interpretation: Assess the supplied technical proposition, rather than merely whether LeCun expressed agreement.

The ordinary reading is that standard language-model training does not by itself deliver reliable commonsense reasoning, physical reasoning and world models. This does not mean literally zero relevant ability.
Interpret 'for free' as without dedicated mechanisms or additional training specifically supplying those capabilities, not without financial or computational cost.

Assess the current state in the latest year-to-date reporting window before the post: January 1 through June 4, 2024. Earlier experiments and later experiments are context unless their timing and applicability can be established.
Do not substitute perfect performance or general intelligence for reliable performance on the stated capabilities.
criteria.support_condition: Applicable evaluations show substantial, repeatable failures in these capabilities in ordinary LLMs, with sufficient training and architecture information to establish that the assessment concerns what ordinary language modeling supplies by itself.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Applicable evaluations show that ordinary language-model training produces reliable, generalizing capabilities across the stated areas without dedicated mechanisms or capability-specific training.

evidence.explanation: ACCORD finds commonsense reasoning becoming unreliable as reasoning complexity increases in GPT-4o, Llama 3 and Mixtral. This supports the reliability concern, but does not test all three capabilities or isolate what pretraining alone supplied.

evidence.locator: Experimental results, Performance of Multimodal Large Language Models
evidence.explanation: ContPhy reports some physical-reasoning strengths alongside substantial weaknesses, especially with deformable objects. These multimodal evaluations caution against an absolute absence claim but do not isolate ordinary text-only language-model training.

evidence.publisher: Wes Gurnee and Max Tegmark, arXiv
evidence.explanation: The study identifies structured spatial and temporal information in Llama 2 representations. It predates the target window and does not establish reliable physical dynamics, but weighs against interpreting 'none' as no learned world structure whatsoever.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled evaluations of models and training methods applicable to the target period, covering all three capabilities with agreed reliability and generalization criteria.
